messages:
arjun: Customer (AcmeCorp) opened a ticket — after enabling SSO their app shows 'Invalid API key' on every request, started ~this morning. They said the session token looks valid and they can hit other vendor APIs with it.

lena: Do we have the raw API response body from our side? Any chance this was an Okta mapping change?

arjun: Pasting the HTTP response they get from our gateway: 
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":"access_denied","message":"Invalid API key"}
```
They also shared the SAML assertion exchange logs — looks like post-auth we create a session token and attach tenant claims. I noticed the transformer log shows claim 'x-redwood-plan' missing for this tenant.

support-bot: ticket CS-7891 created and linked to this thread.

marie: Is AcmeCorp on Redwood Hosted or Private?

arjun: Private (VPC). They run our private control plane in their account; SSO integration is via our SAML endpoint. Repro steps I used locally (customer gave me creds):
1) POST /saml/exchange with SAMLResponse -> returns session token
2) curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://private.api.acme.internal/v1/generate -> 403 above

nate (eng-oncall): That response body is unfortunately generic. Entitlement gating sometimes bubbles up as an auth-style 403 when the transformer/claim lookup fails. I will pull entitlement-service logs for the tenant.

eng-oncall: Found this in entitlement-service logs around the same time: 
```
2026-02-17T12:34:10Z WARN tenant=acmecorp user=admin missing_claim=x-redwood-plan result=DENIED code=403 auth_hint=invalid_credentials_like
```
Looks like the SAML->session mapping returned no plan claim, entitlement lookup returned DENIED, and upstream mapping converted it into the generic invalid-api-key message.

lena: Oof. That would absolutely look like an auth failure to the customer. Root cause = Okta app mapping removed the custom attribute or renamed it?

eng-oncall: Customer confirmed they recently switched to the "Modern SAML" template in Okta; the app integration dropped the custom attribute mapping for x-redwood-plan. Our transformer currently treats missing plan claim as "unknown" and short-circuits with the same error path used for expired/invalid tokens.

marie: Customer admin asked what to change — we should give them exact attribute name and where to add it in Okta. Also need to not surface "Invalid API key" anymore.

arjun: Suggested immediate mitigation to customer: add back attribute mapping named "x-redwood-plan" with their plan slug (e.g., "team-pro"). I also proposed a temporary server-side workaround: we can add a default plan entry on their tenant so requests pass until they fix SAML.

nate: I'll do a scoped hotfix. Plan: (1) patch saml-transformer to return explicit entitlement error codes when claims are missing instead of raising InvalidTokenError, (2) add a tenant-scoped default plan flag we can toggle for AcmeCorp, (3) add telemetry alert for missing x-redwood-plan claims.

support-bot: deploy-bot: rollout started for private-master/us-west-2 (canary tenant: acmecorp).

eng-oncall: Hotfix deployed to the canary and I toggled tenant default-plan=true for AcmeCorp. Confirmed with customer — after a few minutes their requests are succeeding again.

marie: Customer admin re-added the attribute in Okta and confirmed end-to-end. They also asked for clearer errors so internal devs don't burn hours next time.

arjun: Created follow-up tracking ticket PRODX-1120 to standardize entitlement error codes + docs update (SDK error mappings + troubleshooting guide for SSO claim mappings). @nate to own the transformer patch backlog.

nate: I'll file the transformer PR today, add unit tests for missing-claim semantics, and update the error mapping table. Also adding an alert to detect a sudden spike in missing x-redwood-plan claims across tenants.

arjun: Closing loop here — immediate customer impact mitigated via tenant default, Okta mapping fixed by customer, hotfix deployed to make errors clearer. Will keep PRODX-1120 open until docs + backend standardized.

lena: Thanks everyone. Small doc snippet to send to the customer: "If you use SSO, ensure the SAML assertion includes a custom attribute named 'x-redwood-plan' with your plan slug. Missing plan claims will be treated as an entitlement mismatch. If you still see an 'Invalid API key' error after adding the claim, ping support with a sample SAMLResponse and timestamp."

arjun: sending that now to the customer thread and attaching CS-7891. :white_check_mark:
